conviction_note: Four of five filed items point to a transaction-services (Temu) revenue shortfall against a ~RMB117bn bar that assumes Q2's +13% TS growth repeats on a much harder base in the first full quarter of the EU EUR 3 parcel duty; but every item is a proxy or arithmetic, consensus revenue was already cut ~4.7% in three months, the profit line (which PDD has beaten while missing revenue) is unread, and a domestic peer (JD marketplace/marketing +9.6%) cuts the other way, so p_up sits only at 44 on a 7.5% absolute move; the findings sum (-2.2) is larger than the scaled number (-0.9) because the per-finding sizes are each finding alone while p_up carries the uncertainty about profit and reaction.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus ~RMB117.1bn, EPS ~RMB19.21/ADS (Chartmill, snippet_only, 'revised downward 4.72% in the past 3 months', https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/PDD/estimates); Benzinga/Earnings Whispers $17.65bn revenue, EPS $2.36-2.43 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PDD/earnings-forecasts, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/PDD). At the ~6.70 CNY/USD implied by JD's 2026-11-17 6-K the two revenue figures agree within ~1% (RMB117-118bn, ~+8.2% y/y on Q3 2025's RMB108.28bn). PDD gives no guidance, so no company bar exists; segment consensus not found.
positioning_check: Short interest ~34.5m shares, ~2.42% of float, ~5.6 days to cover at the 2026-08-21 settlement (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/pdd/shortinterest, snippet_only); no November reading found; not a crowded short. Baseline: 25d skew +1.22 vol pts (mild put premium, 'balanced'), put/call OI 0.79, event-implied move 6.91%, stock 36.7% below its 52-week high and 5.9% above its low, 20d run-up -1.4%. Reaction history (not in baseline, rebuilt from press): Q3 2025 (2025-11-18) ~-6% intraday on EPS beat / revenue miss; Q1 2026 (2026-05-27) ~-10 to -11% on revenue and profit miss; Q2 2026 (2026-08-24) -1.5% close after +3.5% premarket on EPS beat / revenue miss; Q4 2025 (2026-03-25) reaction not reliably sourced.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter of the EU's EUR 3 per-item duty on sub-EUR150 parcels (effective 2026-07-01): Temu sales volumes fell 50% June-to-July (AliExpress -37%, Shein -15%), French customs put EU small-parcel imports down 30-40% since the duty, Temu's French sales fell 38% m/m (units -50%) per Joko, and Sensor Tower put Temu EU MAU -30% y/y in July; against this, ECDB says Temu AOV rose 37% and Temu targets >80% of EU orders from local warehouses by end-2026, and Consumer Edge showed EU growth >60% in May (pre-duty pull-forward that flattered Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Transaction services / Temu-driven revenue misses: Q2 2026 revenue miss (RMB112.4bn vs RMB115.2bn) with EPS beat closed -1.5%; Q1 2026 revenue miss plus profit miss -10 to -11%; Q3 2025 revenue miss with big EPS beat ~-6% intraday.
findings.why_not_priced: The July data are public and the consensus revenue has been cut ~4.7% in three months, so part of this is in the bar; what is not visible is the size of the EU hit in TS for July-September, because PDD does not break out Temu and no August-October Temu EU series was found. If fully priced, consensus would imply TS deceleration from Q2's +13%; at ~RMB117bn it instead implies TS growth roughly held (see next finding).
findings.independence: ECDB transaction-share data via retail-news.de 2026-11-16 (https://retail-news.de/eu-zoll-temu-shein-aliexpress-transaktionen/) and ecomcrew 2026-08-31 (https://www.ecomcrew.com/?p=67616), different data vendors (ECDB, Joko, Sensor Tower). Offset: Sensor Tower US app users +21% y/y Jan-May 2026 (US recovery after de minimis) per searchengineland compilation. Shares the TS line with the base-effect finding below.

findings.finding: Base-effect arithmetic: Q3 2025 had transaction services RMB54.93bn (+10% y/y) and online marketing RMB53.35bn (+8%); Q2 2026's +13% TS growth (RMB54.7bn) came against a Q2 2025 base that grew only +1%. A ~RMB117.1bn consensus (+8.2%) with online marketing at Q2's ~+3.5% requires TS ~RMB62bn (+13%), i.e. a two-year TS stack accelerating from ~14% in Q2 to ~24% in Q3, in the quarter the EU duty bit; repeating 2024's +4% Q2-to-Q3 TS seasonality instead gives total revenue ~RMB112-115bn, 2-4% below the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue has missed on each of the last three sourced prints (Q3 2025, Q1 2026, Q2 2026) and the stock closed lower after each, even when adjusted EPS beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Segment consensus is not published in the wire copy found; the headline consensus just carries Q2-to-Q3 sequential growth (+4.2%) equal to 2025's, when 2025's Q3 TS jump (+13.7% q/q) was the US recovery after the May 2025 tariff truce, a one-time boost. If priced, the consensus would sit nearer RMB113-115bn.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 actuals from itiger (https://www.itiger.com/news/1107976411, 2026-08-24). Inference from PDD's own filings, not a sell-side segment model; partly shares its conclusion with the EU-duty finding but rests on different numbers (base effects, not EU data).

findings.finding: NBS online retail sales of goods decelerated sharply in Q3 2026: H1 +4.8% (RMB6,429.6bn), Jan-Sep +3.8% (RMB9,506.0bn), implying Q3 alone ~+1.8% y/y, and Jan-Oct slowed further to +2.9%; total retail sales were +1.1% in September.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Online marketing growth slowed to ~+3.5% in Q2 2026 (from +8% in Q3 2025); the Q2 print with that slowdown closed -1.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro series, largely priced; the derived Q3 figure (+1.8%) is rarely quoted, and PDD's domestic online marketing line would track it only loosely. Macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by PDD.
findings.independence: H1 release https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202607/t20260717_1964156.html (2026-07-17); Jan-Oct via Trading Economics https://tradingeconomics.com/china/retail-sales-annual/news/601330. Contradicted in part by JD's marketplace revenue (next finding).

findings.finding: JD.com's Q3 2026 6-K (2026-11-17, after PDD last spoke) shows marketplace and marketing revenue +9.6% to RMB28.1bn and general merchandise +8.1%, with JD's operating margin back to 1.7% from -0.4%: domestic merchant ad spend held up and the subsidy war that pressured PDD's peers appears to be easing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history on PDD for a peer's ad-revenue print; PDD's online marketing line was the weak one in Q2 2026 (~+3.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: Landed two days before the print; PDD consensus revision for it would not yet be visible. It is a peer, not a counterparty, and JD's total revenue (+3.5%) undershot its own pre-release growth expectation, so the read-across is mixed.
findings.independence: none (single document); cuts against the NBS finding.

findings.finding: Reaction pattern: PDD has fallen after its last three sourced prints (~-6% intraday Nov 2025, ~-10 to -11% May 2026, -1.5% close Aug 2026), selling off revenue misses even with EPS beats, while management flags continued 'choppiness' from its RMB100bn merchant-support programme; no guidance or buyback has been given to change that reaction function.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As stated: three of three sourced recent prints closed lower; Aug 2026 premarket +3.5% reversed to -1.5% by the close.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is 36.7% off its high and near its 52-week low, so some disappointment is in the price; the skew is only mildly put-leaning (+1.2), which would be larger if a repeat were priced.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans negative, in line with the mild put skew and the long drawdown, so it is partly priced; nothing cuts against the run-up, and short interest (~2.4% of float) is not crowded enough to squeeze.
lessons_applied: Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): EU-duty finding shrunk -1.0 to -0.8 for the offsetting US Temu recovery and the AOV/localisation shift.
Rule 5 (narrow proxy vs company-level peer): NBS macro finding shrunk -0.6 to -0.4 because JD's company-level marketplace revenue (+9.6%) points the other way.
Pessimism artefact (4 of 5 negative): p_up moved 43 to 44, expected_move -1.05 to -0.9.
Rule 6 (bar): checked two revenue sources agree within ~1% at the JD-implied FX rate, so no cap applied; stated in bar.
Rule 7: short interest looked up (2.4% float, not crowded); no shrink for squeeze.
